newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA record earnings exceed expectations.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA record earnings exceed expectations.

text.p: Computer superstore chain CompUSA Inc. Wednesday reported record fiscal fourth-quarter profits that represented a 94 percent increase and beat analysts forecasts, crediting "standout" sales.

The nation's largest computer retailer reported net income of $22.9 million, or 24 cents per share, in the fourth quarter ended June 28 vs. $11.8 million, or 13 cents a share, in the same period a year ago.
Wall Street analysts on average had forecast earnings of 20 cents a share, according to research service First Call.
CompUSA, based in Dallas, said sales surged 23 percent to $1.15 billion in the quarter from $999 million a year ago.
"Our quarterly comparable-store sales were a standout in the industry," Chief Executive Officer James Halpin said in a statement.
Comparable-store sales by the 102 CompUSA stores open a year or more rose 5.9 percent rose 5.9 percent for the fiscal year.
Halpin also pointed to CompUSA's annual operating margin, a measure of efficiency, of over 3 percent.
The company also posted record fiscal 1997 earnings of $93.9 million, or 99 cents a share, a 57 percent jump over the $59.7 million, or 65 cents a share, earned the previous year.
Analysts had predicted annual earnings of 95 cents a share.
CompUSA's sales for the year increased 22 percent to $4.61 billion from $3.8 billion in fiscal 1996.
CompUSA stock rose $1.44 to close at $29.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
